post.description: Starts a session (200). Browsers get an HttpOnly `__Host-session` cookie; native apps pass `"transport": "bearer"` and get the token in the response. After a 202 from `POST /v1/auth/login`: send the challenge token with a code from the authenticator app, a recovery code, or a passkey's response (start it with `POST /v1/auth/login/mfa/passkey`). Each sign-in allows 5 attempts within 5 minutes; each code works once.

GitHub has no ID token for `POST /v1/auth/identities`, so a signed-in user links it through GitHub's page. Call this with the browser's credentials (fetch with `credentials: "include"`); it sets a short-lived cookie in that browser and returns the GitHub URL to open in it. Send the password unless this session verified a second factor in the last 10 minutes. GitHub returns to the callback, which links the GitHub account to this user, only while this session is active, and redirects to `return_to`, or to `return_to#error=<code>` (`identity_in_use`, `unauthenticated`, `invalid_state`, `access_denied`). Nobody is signed in by it.
Put the nonce in Google's or Apple's SDK request, then send the ID token with it to `POST /v1/auth/{provider}/token`. It works once, for 5 minutes.
